scope: Primary-source reading on choosing and pairing type, numerals, optical size and actual font files. Calendar applications are project proposals, not universal rules or user-approved taste.

sources.title: A checklist for choosing type
sources.reading_locator: Whole lesson: purpose and emotion, language, discriminability, family range, optical size, files, spacing and license; official Google Fonts repository content.md.
sources.actual_reading: Read complete public source text and captions. No third-party images retained.
findings: Expressive associations and practical coverage both matter; reactions vary with cultural and personal context.
Check actual files, characters, styles and spacing rather than assuming every subset includes the advertised capabilities.
transfer_conditions: Compare real titles, author names, weekdays and date figures in their separate roles.
A single display weight can serve a short title; an editable series may need greater range.
limitations: The checklist does not select one aesthetic for a book calendar.
A long family menu does not by itself improve a design.

sources.title: Pairing typefaces
sources.reading_locator: Complete lesson and captions: first-family variation, reasons for adding another face, distinction and harmony.
sources.actual_reading: Read complete public source text and captions in the official Google Fonts repository.
findings: First test whether the primary family's weights, styles, widths and sizes already cover the task.
A second family can provide a different context, tone, coverage or feature; shared shape properties can connect distinct roles.
transfer_conditions: Name the second family's task before adding it.
Compare a one-family composition with an explicitly motivated pair using the same content.
limitations: Serif plus sans does not guarantee a successful relationship.
Matching x-height is useful in some cases, not a universal requirement.

sources.title: Pairing typefaces based on their construction using the font matrix
sources.reading_locator: Complete lesson: skeleton/flesh/skin model, three pairing paths, worked comparisons and stated limits.
sources.actual_reading: Read complete official source text and example captions, including exceptions and boundary cases.
findings: Broad serif/sans classification conceals different underlying construction models.
Similar construction or deliberate strong contrast can guide pairing; a superficial resemblance can hide friction.
transfer_conditions: Describe the shared or opposing shape property in actual specimens.
Return to a mixed sentence and the whole page after isolated comparisons.
limitations: The matrix is a heuristic, not a binding creative rule.
Its Latin letterform analysis does not establish a universal taxonomy for Chinese, script or display faces.

sources.title: Choosing typefaces that have optical sizes
sources.reading_locator: Whole lesson, including small/display treatments and viewing-distance example.
sources.actual_reading: Read complete official source text and captions.
findings: Size-specific designs may change width, x-height, contrast and spacing rather than simply scaling outlines.
Viewing distance changes perceived size, so physical artwork size alone is insufficient.
transfer_conditions: Compare supported optical styles or opsz settings at the intended size and distance.
Call manual ink-size matching visual correction when the font has no optical-size mechanism.
limitations: Not every variable font includes opsz.
The two retained Noto files have only wght; weight adjustment is not optical sizing.

sources.title: Understanding numerals
sources.reading_locator: Whole lesson: four figure combinations and their contexts; checked the official numerals/figures glossary too.
sources.actual_reading: Read complete lesson and glossary text in the official Google Fonts repository.
findings: Lining versus oldstyle and tabular versus proportional describe separate properties.
Aligned changing values can benefit from tabular figures; running text may use different rhythmic choices.
transfer_conditions: Compare dense year grids, seven-day annotations and a large single date separately.
Verify both the font's feature support and the renderer's actual use of the selected feature.
limitations: A font may not contain every combination.
A feature tag or default advance measurement does not prove a rendered export enables that feature.

sources.title: IBM Design Language – Type scale
sources.reading_locator: Type scale equation, Adjusted scale, and introduction to Large formats.
sources.actual_reading: Selected sections read; not all templates or tables were downloaded or studied.
findings: IBM coordinates font size, line height, script adjustments and large-format viewing within one brand system.
Its 95% script adjustment has an explicit system context.
transfer_conditions: Record relationships between roles and change them with output format or viewing distance.
Check actual Chinese and Latin ink size before making script-specific corrections.
limitations: IBM's 95% value and size sequence are brand requirements, not universal calendar ratios.
Different fonts and content need renewed evaluation.

sources.title: IBM Design Language – Typeface
sources.reading_locator: Subfamilies, type tester, features, mono versus sans, language support, and license sections.
sources.actual_reading: Selected official sections read; no claim to all downstream language packages or releases.
findings: The system connects subfamilies to roles and supports testing actual text.
The Mono design's 600-unit width and the wider family's language support are different levels of information.
transfer_conditions: Try related subfamilies for role contrast, then inspect the precise file's coverage and features.
Use real calendar text in the specimen rather than a family name alone.
limitations: A multilingual family description does not mean the retained Plex Mono or Sans Condensed file contains Chinese.
A brand's code-font recommendation is not a default rule for date figures.

sources.title: Size-specific adjustments to type designs
sources.reading_locator: Public purpose, optical-size definition, research motivation/method, features and contents; Tim Ahrens and Shoko Mugikura.
sources.actual_reading: Read public introduction and contents only; the paid book was not read in full.
findings: The authors frame size-specific changes through historical specimens, designer interviews and comparative form study.
Shape, contrast, width, spacing and alternatives are separate areas of investigation.
transfer_conditions: Vary one typographic property in a short specimen, identify its viewing problem, then inspect the whole page.
limitations: A book introduction cannot substitute for its full argument or results.
The public page does not license its book pages, illustrations or commercial fonts for templates.

non_claims: These sources do not establish a user's aesthetic preference.
Font availability is separate from implemented shaping, feature selection and export fidelity.
Research references are not automatically reusable design assets.
